beats.text: The real Uncle Tom led 118 people to freedom.

overlays.hook: The real "Uncle Tom" *led 118 people to freedom.*

beats.text: Born enslaved in Maryland in 1789, he saw his family sold at auction as a boy.
He grew up to run his enslaver's farm. In 1825, he was sent to lead eighteen enslaved people to Kentucky.
He had been promised his freedom. He saved 350 dollars to buy himself.
His enslaver changed the price to 1,000. Then Henson learned he would be sold to New Orleans, away from his wife and children.
So in 1830, he ran. He crossed the free states with his wife and children, carrying the smallest ones.
On October 28, 1830, they reached Canada. Free.
There he helped build the Dawn Settlement, a community and a school for people who had escaped slavery.
And he kept going back. By his own count, he guided 118 people to freedom.
In 1849, he published his life story. Many believe it inspired Uncle Tom's Cabin.
Today Uncle Tom is an insult. The man behind the name was anything but.

facts.claim: Born enslaved 15 June 1789, Charles County, Maryland; family sold apart at auction.
Became supervisor of Isaac Riley's farm; in 1825 led 18 enslaved people to Kentucky.
Promised manumission; saved $350 to buy himself.
Riley altered the price to $1,000; Henson was to be sold in New Orleans away from wife and four children.
1830 escape with wife and children; carried the smallest.
Dawn Settlement and British-American Institute near Dresden, Ontario.
By his own count, guided 118 people to freedom.
1849 autobiography; widely considered an inspiration for Uncle Tom's Cabin (1852).
